17: # OpenCode CLI - Install and Version Layouts
18: 
19: How to put OpenCode 2.1.4 on a machine, optionally alongside OpenCode 1.19.4 as a fallback, and how to tell which version a name runs.
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 1. OVERVIEW
24: 
25: ### Purpose
26: 
27: This reference is the skill's install guidance. OpenCode 2 is the version this repository expects and recommends; OpenCode 1 is a backwards-compatible fallback kept only because not every user has updated yet. A dispatch needs a known binary, and the two supported majors are separate npm packages that both claim the name `opencode`.
28: 
29: ### When to Use
30: 
31: - Installing OpenCode 2.1.4, alone or side by side with the `opencode1` launcher for v1
32: - Installing OpenCode 1.19.4 alone or side by side, the fallback path for users who have not updated
33: - Deciding whether Homebrew, mise or a second npm prefix is the right channel
34: - Working out why a bare `opencode` runs the version you did not expect
35: 
36: ### Claim Labels
37: 
38: Claims in the prose carry one of three labels. The layout table in section 3 summarises the sections below it, whose claims are labelled there.
39: 
40: | Label | Meaning |
41: |-------|---------|
42: | `[confirmed]` | Observed on this machine on 2026-10-18 with the command named in the sentence. |
43: | `[documented]` | Stated by a named source: the official v2 docs at [https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/), the launcher comment in `~/.local/bin/opencode1`, the CLI's own `--help` output, or the npm registry. |
44: | `[unknown]` | Not probed. Treat it as open and do not plan around it. |
45: 
46: ### The Fact Behind Every Collision
47: 
48: Both majors ship a binary named `opencode` [confirmed: `npm view opencode-ai bin` returns `{ opencode: 'bin/opencode.exe' }` and `npm view @opencode/cli bin` returns `{ opencode: 'bin/opencode.exe', opencode2: 'bin/opencode.exe' }`]. One prefix therefore cannot hold both versions under that name. v2 is the expected version, so it keeps the name `opencode`, and v1 is the one that moves: side by side it answers only to the `opencode1` launcher. The second v2 name, `opencode2`, is retired in that layout.
49: 
50: ### Key Sources
51: 
52: | Source | What it gives you |
53: |--------|-------------------|
54: | `~/.local/bin/opencode1` | The v1 launcher that keeps the two databases apart |
55: | [https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/) | The official v2 install channels and the v2 platform docs |
56: | `../scripts/opencode-setup.sh` | The helper that builds any of the three layouts |
57: | `./cli-reference.md` | Subcommands, `run` flags and the version-drift section |
58: 
59: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 2.1.4 and OpenCode 1.19.4 on 2026-10-24. Flag and provider observations that name 2.0.32 or 1.19.3 were read on those releases and have not been re-read on 2.1.4 or 1.19.4. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in this reference.
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: ## 2. PREREQUISITES
64: 
65: ### Tooling
66: 
67: - Node.js and npm for every npm layout. The npm on this machine is `/opt/homebrew/bin/npm` 11.19.1 [confirmed: `command -v npm` and `npm -v`].
68: - A POSIX shell for the launcher, which is `/bin/sh` [confirmed: the launcher's shebang].
69: - macOS or Linux. The npm path is cross-platform. The Homebrew channels are not.
70: 
71: ### Pinned Targets
72: 
73: | Version | Package | Pin | Channel `latest` |
74: |---------|---------|-----|------------------|
75: | v2 (recommended) | `@opencode/cli` | `2.1.4` | `2.1.4` |
76: | v1 (fallback) | `opencode-ai` | `1.19.4` | `1.19.4` |
77: 
78: Each pin is its package's current `latest` [confirmed: `npm view @opencode/cli dist-tags` and `npm view opencode-ai dist-tags`, read 2026-10-24]. The v1 package was not moved to 2.x, so a v1 package update cannot drift a v1 install into v2 [confirmed: `opencode-ai`'s `latest` dist-tag is 1.19.4].
79: 
80: ### Read First
81: 
82: The name collision in "The Fact Behind Every Collision" decides almost every choice below. If you are adding a second version to a machine that already has one, read section 3 before you run any install command.
83: 
84: ---
85: 
86: ## 3. INSTALLATION
87: 
88: ### The Three Layouts
89: 
90: Read the warning in a layout's own section before you run its command. The v2 layouts come first because OpenCode 2 is the recommended target; the v1-only layout is the fallback for users who have not updated. Each row takes the `opencode` name: the v2 rows orphan or shadow an existing v1 install, and the v1 row collides with a v2 `opencode` already on `PATH`.

16: # OpenCode CLI - Complete Command Reference
17: 
18: Comprehensive reference for the OpenCode CLI binary, every subcommand the cli-opencode skill dispatches against, the flag set it relies on, the agent surface it can target and the failure modes that need explicit handling. Version baselines: OpenCode 2 at 2.1.4, the recommended target, and OpenCode 1 at 1.19.4, the backwards-compatible fallback for users who have not updated.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Provide a single-source reference for the OpenCode CLI surface: every subcommand cli-opencode invokes, every flag it pins, every agent it can route to, the version baselines it is built against and the error envelopes that need explicit recovery.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: - Looking up an OpenCode CLI subcommand or flag during a delegation
31: - Selecting a model + variant + agent for a dispatch
32: - Confirming the version baseline before pinning a flag set
33: - Troubleshooting a failed `opencode run` invocation
34: - Confirming the self-invocation guard signal against the live binary
35: 
36: ### Core Principle
37: 
38: OpenCode is the framework that owns this repository. The same binary that hosts the operator's TUI session also accepts non-interactive invocations through `opencode run`. The cli-opencode skill calls `opencode run` from external runtimes (Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot, raw shell) so the calling AI can dispatch a task into a fresh OpenCode session that loads the full plugin, skill, and MCP runtime.
39: 
40: ### Key Sources
41: 
42: | Source | URL |
43: |--------|-----|
44: | **Binary** | `opencode` for OpenCode 2, the recommended target; side by side, the OpenCode 1 fallback is `opencode1`, and a v1-only machine names it `opencode`. With no `OPENCODE_BIN`, resolution takes the first `opencode2` anywhere on `PATH` and only falls back to the first `opencode` in `PATH` order when none exists |
45: | **Repository** | [sst/opencode](https://github.com/sst/opencode) |
46: | **Version baseline** | OpenCode 2 (recommended): 2.1.4 |
47: | **Version baseline** | OpenCode 1 (fallback): 1.19.4 |
48: | **Runtime** | Node.js 18+ for the npm install path or the standalone binary on macOS |
49: 
50: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 2.1.4 and OpenCode 1.19.4 on 2026-10-24. Flag and provider observations that name 2.0.32 or 1.19.3 were read on those releases and have not been re-read on 2.1.4 or 1.19.4. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).

16: # OpenCode CLI - Complete Command Reference
17: 
18: Comprehensive reference for the OpenCode CLI binary, every subcommand the cli-opencode skill dispatches against, the flag set it relies on, the agent surface it can target and the failure modes that need explicit handling. Version baselines: OpenCode 2 at 2.1.4, the recommended target, and OpenCode 1 at 1.19.4, the backwards-compatible fallback for users who have not updated.

22: ## 1. OVERVIEW
23: 
24: ### Purpose
25: 
26: Provide a single-source reference for the OpenCode CLI surface: every subcommand cli-opencode invokes, every flag it pins, every agent it can route to, the version baselines it is built against and the error envelopes that need explicit recovery.
27: 
28: ### When to Use
29: 
30: - Looking up an OpenCode CLI subcommand or flag during a delegation
31: - Selecting a model + variant + agent for a dispatch
32: - Confirming the version baseline before pinning a flag set
33: - Troubleshooting a failed `opencode run` invocation
34: - Confirming the self-invocation guard signal against the live binary
35: 
36: ### Core Principle
37: 
38: OpenCode is the framework that owns this repository. The same binary that hosts the operator's TUI session also accepts non-interactive invocations through `opencode run`. The cli-opencode skill calls `opencode run` from external runtimes (Claude Code, OpenCode, Copilot, raw shell) so the calling AI can dispatch a task into a fresh OpenCode session that loads the full plugin, skill, and MCP runtime.
39:

43: |--------|-----|
44: | **Binary** | `opencode` for OpenCode 2, the recommended target; side by side, the OpenCode 1 fallback is `opencode1`, and a v1-only machine names it `opencode`. With no `OPENCODE_BIN`, resolution takes the first `opencode2` anywhere on `PATH` and only falls back to the first `opencode` in `PATH` order when none exists |
45: | **Repository** | [sst/opencode](https://github.com/sst/opencode) |
46: | **Version baseline** | OpenCode 2 (recommended): 2.1.4 |
47: | **Version baseline** | OpenCode 1 (fallback): 1.19.4 |
48: | **Runtime** | Node.js 18+ for the npm install path or the standalone binary on macOS |
49: 
50: **Verified versions.** Verified against OpenCode 2.1.4 and OpenCode 1.19.4 on 2026-10-24. Flag and provider observations that name 2.0.32 or 1.19.3 were read on those releases and have not been re-read on 2.1.4 or 1.19.4. Loads and runs on both, with a documented capability delta. Later versions are unsupported until re-verified. The delta is in [`install-and-versions.md`](./install-and-versions.md).

 ## 2. OVERVIEW
 
-### Why This Skill Exists
-
-An external session that needs the project's whole runtime has no native path to get it. Every plugin and skill, the registered MCP servers, the spec folders and their continuity docs: none of that loads from outside. Hand-building an `opencode run` invocation hits the non-obvious traps. The dispatch hangs at zero percent CPU when stdin stays open. The current OpenCode rejects a top-level `--agent general` without saying why. A caller that is itself OpenCode risks a self-dispatch loop that burns tokens. This skill standardizes the dispatch across the documented use cases and refuses self-invocation.
-
 ### What It Does
 
 cli-opencode is the single routing point for runtimes that need an OpenCode dispatch. 170: - **Fallback**: fall back to the flash default `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` — the default on both OpenCode versions — only with Layers 1+2+3 all in place.

418: The bug is in opencode v1.14.39. The fix would be: in the `run` subcommand entrypoint, check `process.stdin.isTTY` (or equivalent) and skip the stdin read in non-interactive mode. The message is already provided as a positional argument, so stdin is informational only. Until upstream patches this, `</dev/null` at every callsite is the workaround. 420: ---
421: 
422: ## 7. MEMORY HANDBACK
423: 
424: cli-opencode dispatches that produce evidence for a `/speckit:save` continuity write MUST include the Memory Epilogue at the end of the prompt. The dispatched session adds `MEMORY_HANDBACK_START` / `MEMORY_HANDBACK_END` delimiters around a structured JSON payload that the calling AI extracts and feeds to `generate-context.js`.
425: 
426: The full Memory Handback Protocol is shared with cli-claude-code and cli-opencode. See SKILL.md Section 4 (RULES) for the canonical 7-step procedure. The same JSON normalization (camelCase / snake_case aliases) and save gates apply.
427: 
428: ---
429: 
430: ## 8. SINGLE-DISPATCH DISCIPLINE
431: 
432: **Single-dispatch discipline (operator-gated, session-scoped).**
433: 
434: - **Default**: launch ONE cli-* dispatch at a time across the cli-* family (cli-opencode, cli-claude-code). Wait for the work to return, verify outputs exist.
435: - **Kill only the dispatch THIS skill started**: capture its PID at launch (`opencode run ... & OC_PID=$!`) and SIGKILL that captured PID directly plus its own orphan children (`kill -9 "$OC_PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$OC_PID" 2>/dev/null`), then apply the same PID-scoped `gtimeout` / `positional_scoring_fallback:app` cleanup. (A backgrounded `opencode run &` is not a process-group leader, so a group kill would miss it. Kill the captured PID directly.)
436: - **Never blanket-kill**: never a blanket `pkill -9 -f "opencode run"` pattern (see Rule 5), which kills operator-owned sessions too.
437: - **Before the next dispatch**: only launch the next dispatch (this skill OR a sibling) after the prior one is dead and RSS has dropped.
438: - **Deep-flow session** (deep-review / deep-research): the operator authorizes the whole session at start, and iterations chain back-to-back with kill-between as the safety mechanism, NOT a per-iteration confirmation prompt.
439: - **Exception (cross-skill parallel)**: when the operator explicitly authorizes N parallel dispatches, run N concurrently, but still SIGKILL each by its own captured PID as its work returns.
